sections.text: Level 1 version gives the room the format. Level 4 version gives that format the authority to feel like a serious dedicated cinema. Where maximum performance and headroom are the priority, Level 4 version is the stronger recommendation.

Both options use the same room dimensions, the same 185" (2.35:1) screen and the same 9.1.6 (15 discrete channels) layout. The seating and Artcoustic Abfuser × 8 treatment are also shared, so the comparison is about the equipment and the performance each option delivers within this common design.

The loudspeaker package changes between options. Level 4 version uses Q8-5 × 3 for the screen, Q6-3 × 6 for surrounds and wides, and SPITFIRE CLOUD × 6 overhead; Level 1 version uses Q6-3 × 3, EVOLVE 2-1 × 6 and ARCHITECT 2-1 × 6 in those roles. The subwoofer specification also changes: SUB4-12 × 2 (front), SUB4-12 × 2 (rear) in Level 4 version, compared with SUB4-12 (front), SUB4-12 (rear) in Level 1 version. The recorded performance gains and trade-offs are set out below.

The principal gains for Level 4 version are in dynamic range: the screen stage, the surround and height layers, and the subwoofer system each have a material gain recorded. Level 1 version has the higher recorded result for bass extension. Both options record the same result for screen and surround/overhead tonal consistency; bass consistency remains Level 1 in both.

Both options place the same sound positions around and above the seats. The front wide positions bridge the screen and side speakers more effectively in Level 1 version; the recorded levels are L3 for Level 1 version and L2 for Level 4 version. Screen-channel level across the seats, listener-level speaker spacing and overhead spacing are all recorded at the same level in both options, with no material difference. Viewing angles are calculated for 9 seats, and both options have a primary floor of L3.

Level 4 version has more front-stage headroom, giving dialogue, score and screen effects more room to expand before the system sounds strained. It also has more capability around and above the seating, helping surround and height effects keep their presence during demanding scenes. Its subwoofer result supports more bass authority and physical impact for film soundtracks. Level 1 version has usable headroom in the surround and height layers, with less reserve than the screen stage.

Both options record tonal consistency across the screen channels, so voices and effects stay consistent from left to right. Tonal consistency around and above the seats is also recorded in both, supporting consistency as effects move through the room. Level 1 version records the higher level for bass extension, describing how far down the system reaches for the lowest film effects. Bass consistency remains Level 1 in both options; bass output authority is the area where Level 4 version gains.

Level 1 version remains a credible 9.1.6 design. The distinction is not the format, but the greater headroom and authority recorded for Level 4 version, alongside changes to the loudspeaker and subwoofer package. Level 4 version is the stronger recommendation where maximum performance and headroom are the priority; the bass results do not indicate improved seat-to-seat consistency.

This comparison is based on the saved visual and technical report evidence for Level 4 version and Level 1 version. The report snapshots are visual 6ac20c15df233b979449bcc3 and technical 6ac391ef796c4899260e0c5a for Level 4 version, and visual 6ac2257837dd624e74adf140 and technical 6ac275599f85fb8449ec3fd2 for Level 1 version.
